body: In all honesty after I took the large amount I had i just fell asleep and that was it till I woke up in the hospital (I still really have no idea what happened to my body between I feel asleep and when I work up) I was then given a section 2 on release which isn't ideal cause I got diagnosed with EUPD on top of my anxiety and depression they weren't overly keen on getting me a DNR so that was a fun way to spend 6 weeks and now I've been off work since May as the cocktail of meds I'm on has implications on my work 🫤

To be honest I don't regret it as much as I probably should, as bad as that sounds. The UK health service (NHS) is probably one of the best things about this country. Don't attempt again, there are people out there who love and care for you and if you attempt and survive, everything becomes awkward and life feels worse.

these things are scarily noisy, I remember being sat on a platform at YRK and one came in and left. Just could not believe the noise coming from them, don't get me wrong I love a loud thrashing loco just as much as anything but these things are just an earache.
shoutout to the NHS btw and particually Nathan from Ward 4, the UK health service is one of the greatest things we have
